A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page documents, including their appendices. Despite the change from SimLayerKV to LightTransfer and substantial expansion, they retain the same lazy-layer observation and selective KV-cache reduction foundation, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench and RULER evaluations, layer-selection ablations, and additional model experiments in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 reports original long-context and mathematical-reasoning evaluations, throughput measurements, hyperparameter ablations, and SnapKV combination experiments.

M1.justification: v1 identifies lazy layers using thresholds during prefilling or the first decoding step. v2 replaces this selection rule with a budgeted priority queue during prefilling and introduces FlashAttention log-sum-exp-based scoring. LightTransfer-Train additionally selects layers by frequency across training examples and fine-tunes the resulting hybrid architecture, substantially extending the training-free procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds short-input, long-reasoning training and evaluation on MATH-OAI, AIME24 and GSM8K. Its RULER evaluation narrows to single-key and multiple-key NIAH, omitting v1's multiple-value/query retrieval, aggregation, QA and variable-tracking scenarios. The five additional LongBench tasks reported in v1 Appendix A.3 are also no longer reported.

E2.justification: v2 adds SqueezeAttention to the main LongBench comparison and evaluates LongGen alongside QwQ-STILL in the new reasoning experiments; LongGen was only cited in v1. MiniCache disappears from the retained NIAH comparison, and quantized MiniCache comparisons are removed. SnapKV remains evaluated, but the appendix comparison now tests SnapKV combined with LightTransfer.

E3.justification: The model-specific thresholds in v1 are replaced by fixed layer budgets: 50% standard layers on LongBench and 25% layer removal on NIAH. The recent-token window changes from 1024 to 1020. v2 adds LLaMA3-70B and reasoning-model configurations, approximately 5K-example fine-tuning with a 32K generation limit, and throughput testing at maximum feasible batch sizes; Yi-9B evaluation is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of retained-layer fraction, sink-token count, recent-window size, identification-query count, and combining LightTransfer with SnapKV. It also examines layer scores in the reasoning model. v1's separate lazy-versus-non-lazy trimming experiment, threshold sweep, and prefilling-versus-decoding comparison disappear; the Pyramid/Random strategy comparison survives with revised coverage and presentation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's deterministic approximation-error bounds are theoretical results, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous LongBench scores are replaced: the proposed method's Mistral average changes from 44.2 in v1 Table 1 to 47.4 in v2 Table 2, under revised methods/settings rather than an established same-setting gain. v2 adds 53.3% AIME24 accuracy and throughput reaching 2.17 times Standard, while removing quantization and broader RULER results. Its multiple-key NIAH plot conflicts with the accompanying numerical passage, leaving that revised series unresolved.

T1.justification: v1 provides algorithmic definitions without approximation guarantees or proofs. v2 adds Theorem 5.1, a formal hidden-state error recurrence and logit-error bound in Theorem F.3, bounded-parameter and Lipschitz assumptions, transformer/masking definitions, and proofs and supporting lemmas in Appendices E–G.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a seven-line, training-free KV-cache compressor claiming approximately fivefold compression with quantization to lightweight transformer-to-hybrid conversion with separate test-time and fine-tuned variants. v2's abstract and conclusion emphasize measured throughput, retained long-context performance, and mathematical reasoning, substantially broadening the contribution beyond v1's compression claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of why short prompts prevent reliable lazy-ratio identification, why fine-tuning is needed, and why tensor-parallel execution discourages head-wise conversion. It attributes performance to controlling an error bound and claims hyperparameter robustness. v1's explanations of multiple-query retrieval and aggregation failures disappear, while its untested-combination limitation is partly addressed by the SnapKV experiment.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the two cache-trimming pseudocode blocks with FlashAttention lazy-ratio code and identifies FlexAttention and QwQ-STILL training data for the new training branch. The direct GitHub code link becomes a project-homepage link. These are limited implementation/access-information revisions; detailed fine-tuning optimizer and schedule settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: The KV-cache-compression positioning is substantially recast around hybrid architectures and lightweight transformer conversion. v2 adds extensive discussion and citations involving Mamba, Jamba, YoCo, MiniMax-01 and conversion/distillation approaches. LongGen, already cited in v1, becomes a central contrast concerning fixed layer selection and adaptation requirements.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, related work and much of the methodological and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around LightTransfer and its two variants. The appendices are reorganized from A.1–A.4 into separate settings, discussions, experiments, examples, notation and proof sections. This exceeds simple renaming or adding sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. Earlier attention visualizations are combined in v2 Figure 2, new architecture and priority-queue diagrams appear, and the LongBench table is regrouped and shaded. The broad RULER table becomes two NIAH plots, alongside new reasoning, throughput and hyperparameter displays.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies measured throughput for v1's acceleration claim and adds useful comparison, reasoning and theoretical evidence. However, it removes informative RULER failure tests and discussion, and introduces consequential inconsistencies: Figure 4(b) plots roughly 96–97% at 32K while Section 6.1.2 reports 78.2%/78.9%; Table 5 reports 26.5 versus 39.8 despite claiming variation within one percentage point. These unresolved reliability issues and coverage losses prevent a confident net quality judgment despite the substantive additions.
